label: Hydrolagus colliei
summary: Holostylic: the palatoquadrate is fused to the braincase, so there is no free upper jaw to protrude, and the muscles that move one are gone. Only the lower jaw swings. Mouth-region movement is taken up instead by a set of labial cartilages.
note: Outlines, lever arms and ranges of motion are schematic. The muscles, attachments and credited actions come from Huber et al. (2011) Table 4 and its text, and the absences from Anderson (2008); tests/sim.test.js checks the geometry against them. The fused palatoquadrate is drawn as a separate shape so the missing joint is visible. The opercular constrictors are drawn as one dorsoventral chord because the dorsal and ventral muscles share an insertion on the opercular sheath, and the flap really closes by swinging inward, out of the plane of this view. The labial cartilages are one piece sliding forward and back.

tr-d.label: Vertebral column and pectoral girdle (origin of the dorsal opercular constrictor)

gl-v.label: Midventral raphe (origin of the ventral opercular constrictor)

mk-am1.label: Meckel's cartilage (tendon wraps beneath the lower jaw)

mk-am2.label: Meckel's cartilage (tendon merges with the anterior division's)

muscles.label: Adductor mandibulae anterior
muscles.actionText: Closes the lower jaw. Broad origin across the preorbital chondrocranium and a stout tendon that wraps beneath the jaw; the primary adductor.

muscles.label: Adductor mandibulae posterior
muscles.actionText: Closes the lower jaw. From the suborbital ridge; its tendon merges with the anterior division's.

muscles.label: Coracomandibularis
muscles.actionText: Opens the lower jaw, from the coracoid bar to the jaw.
muscles.note: Anderson (2008) argues that jaw depression in this lineage worked directly through this muscle, and that the ratfish also has a second route (his mandibulohyoideus).

muscles.label: Coracohyoideus
muscles.actionText: Depresses the hyoid arch, acting on the basihyal.

muscles.label: Levator hyoideus
muscles.actionText: From the underside of the chondrocranium beneath the orbit onto the epihyal; lifts the epihyal.
muscles.note: Parked in the dataset: whether it is the levator hyomandibulae of the other two animals is not settled, and it is not drawn as that muscle here.

muscles.label: Intermandibularis
muscles.actionText: From the inferior maxillary cartilage to the premandibular cartilages at the jaw symphysis; protracts the labial cartilages.
muscles.note: Not a floor-of-the-mouth elevator as in the shark: here the same muscle works the lip.

muscles.label: Levator anguli oris
muscles.actionText: From the antorbital crest to the superior maxillary cartilage; retracts the labial cartilages through ligaments.

muscles.label: Opercular constrictors (dorsal + ventral)
muscles.actionText: The dorsal division from the vertebral column and pectoral girdle and the ventral from the midventral raphe share an insertion on the opercular sheath; together they squeeze the pharyngeal cavity.
muscles.note: Both are parked in the dataset without a record.

muscles.label: Levator palatoquadrati
muscles.reason: Anderson (2008) reads it as a secondary loss: the palatoquadrate is fused to the braincase, so there is nothing free to lift.

muscles.label: Interhyoideus
muscles.actionText: Huber et al. describe an interhyoideus from the jaw symphysis to the ceratohyals that abducts the hyoid arch.
muscles.reason: Anderson (2008) finds no homologous interhyoideus in this animal and reads a secondary loss; Huber et al.'s muscle of that name is parked in the dataset as unresolved. Not drawn.

muscles.label: Epibranchial (epaxial) muscle
muscles.actionText: Inserts on the chondrocranium but contributes little to head lift.
muscles.reason: The holocephalan braincase is relatively akinetic, so no cranial-lift joint is modelled.
